attachments.origin_landmark: highest nuchal line and the mastoid process (occipital belly)
attachments.insertion_landmark: skin of the eyebrow and root of the nose, via the galea aponeurotica (frontal belly)

actions: raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead

functional_compartments.name: Frontal belly (venter frontalis)
functional_compartments.function_note: Has no bony attachment at all -- it arises entirely from the galea aponeurotica and inserts into skin. Forehead sparing in an upper motor neuron facial palsy reflects its bilateral cortical innervation, and is the single most useful sign separating a stroke from Bell's palsy.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

functional_compartments.name: Occipital belly (venter occipitalis)
functional_compartments.function_note: Anchors the galea posteriorly so the frontal belly has something to pull against.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
